title: STRIDE: Automated Evaluation of Text-to-Trajectory Alignment across Diverse Contexts
abstract: arXiv:2609.34799v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language-conditioned trajectory generation is here, but its evaluation has not kept pace. Existing pedestrian trajectory metrics compare trajectories with real-world human data. This does not scale to text-to-trajectory generation across diverse contexts, as collecting human trajectories for every scenario is costly and infeasible. Moreover, pedestrian behavior is heterogeneous and context-dependent, with no single metric as the correct answer, and current evaluation frameworks are not transferable to this domain. These challenges make scalable, reliable evaluation difficult. We introduce STRIDE, the first framework for evaluating context alignment between scenario descriptions and pedestrian trajectories. STRIDE addresses these challenges through three design choices. First, we derive our VRDST evaluation protocol from sociological theories to define a complete evaluation space. Second, it decomposes high-level context into scenario

translated_title: STRIDE：面向多样化情境的文本-轨迹对齐自动化评估
translated_abstract: 语言条件化的轨迹生成已经问世，但其评估方法却未能跟上步伐。现有的行人轨迹指标是将生成轨迹与真实世界的人类数据进行比较。这种方法无法扩展到跨多样化情境的文本到轨迹生成任务，因为为每个场景收集人类轨迹既昂贵又不可行。此外，行人行为具有异质性且依赖于具体情境，不存在单一的“正确答案”式指标，而当前的评估框架也无法迁移到这一领域。这些挑战使得可扩展且可靠的评估变得十分困难。我们提出了STRIDE，这是首个用于评估场景描述与行人轨迹之间情境对齐程度的框架。STRIDE通过三项设计选择来应对这些挑战。首先，我们从社会学理论中推导出VRDST评估协议，以定义完整的评估空间。其次，它将高层次情境分解为场景……
tldr: 该论文提出首个评估场景文本描述与行人轨迹之间情境对齐的自动化框架STRIDE，通过源自社会学理论的VRDST评估协议，解决了传统依赖真实人类数据的评估方法在多样化情境下无法扩展的难题。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces STRIDE, the first framework for automated evaluation of context alignment between scenario descriptions and pedestrian trajectories, addressing the scalability limitations of traditional human-data-based metrics through a sociologically-derived VRDST evaluation protocol across diverse contexts.
